label: pit-
meaning: a portion of land, farm (Pictish pett)

label: betws
meaning: chapel, prayer house (Welsh betws, from Old English bedhus)

label: -ton
meaning: farmstead, estate, later village (Old English tun). Some -ston names are stan, stone

label: -ley / -leigh
meaning: woodland clearing, later meadow (Old English leah)

label: -ing / -ings
meaning: the people of, or place of (Old English -ingas, -ing)

label: -ham
meaning: homestead, village (Old English ham); some are hamm, land in a river bend, which the spelling cannot separate

label: -ford
meaning: ford, a river crossing (Old English ford)

label: -field
meaning: open land, cleared country (Old English feld)

label: -town
meaning: town, farm or settlement (later English town, from Old English tun)

label: -bury / -borough
meaning: fortified place, later manor or town (Old English burh); some -borough names are beorg, hill

label: -den / -dean
meaning: valley (denu) or woodland pasture for pigs (denn), Old English

label: -wick / -wich
meaning: specialised farm (often a dairy farm) or trading place (Old English wic, from Latin vicus)

label: -stow
meaning: place, often a holy place or meeting place (Old English stow)

label: -minster
meaning: monastery or major church (Old English mynster)

label: bally- / bal-
meaning: baile: farm, homestead, settlement. In Irish names Bally- can also be beal atha, ford mouth

label: kil- / kill-
meaning: cill: church. Kil- can also be coill, wood, and other words

label: dun- / dum-
meaning: dun: fort, stronghold. Irish Don- is often domhnach, church

label: bel- / bella-
meaning: beal: mouth, approach (often to a ford)

label: -chester / -caster
meaning: Old English ceaster, a Roman fort or town (from Latin castra)

label: strat- / stret-
meaning: Old English straet, a paved road, often Roman (from Latin strata)

label: eccles-
meaning: church, from Brittonic, from Latin ecclesia

label: -thorpe
meaning: outlying farm (Old Norse thorp; a few are Old English throp)

label: -holme / -holm
meaning: island, dry ground in marsh, water meadow (Old Norse holmr)

label: kirk-
meaning: church (Old Norse kirkja). Counted in England only, because Scots kirk is an everyday word

label: -toft
meaning: site of a house, homestead (Old Norse topt)
